maker.name: Cherry
maker.about: Founded in 1953 by Walter Lorain Cherry in Highland Park, Illinois, and now based in Auerbach in der Oberpfalz, Germany. Its MX switch was developed and patented in the early 1980s and first marketed around 1985.

switches.name: MX Black Clear-Top

reviews.verdict: Big gains over stock Cherry linears in scratch, spring ping and wobble; the unlubed version keeps some scratch and a thin top-out.

sources.title: Cherry: MX Black Clear-Top product page
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Clear Top Switches
ThereminGoat: Cherry MX 'New Nixie' Switch Review

switches.notes: Cherry calls it a re-release of the 1980s MX Nixie made for Nixdorf; sold unlubed (MX1A-61NW) and pre-lubed.

switches.name: MX Clear
switches.notes: Classic MX1A part numbers (MX1A-C1xx), in RGB and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX Green
switches.notes: Classic MX1A part numbers (MX1A-F1xx); a two-part stem produces the click.

switches.name: MX RGB Nature White
switches.notes: Linear between MX Red and MX Black, part MX1A-41NA; last order date 24 September 2019 per telcontar.net. Retailers still list remaining stock.

switches.name: MX Tactile Grey
switches.notes: Classic MX1A part numbers (MX1A-D1xx), in RGB and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX Low Profile Red

sources.title: Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Low Profile

switches.notes: Part MX1B-L2NA, shown at CES 2018 and used in keyboards such as the Cooler Master SK630. Cherry now lists only the Low Profile 2.0 versions.

switches.name: MX Low Profile Speed

sources.title: Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Low Profile

switches.notes: Part MX1B-52NA, first sold through Corsair keyboards such as the K70 MK.2 Low Profile. Cherry now lists only the Low Profile 2.0 versions.

switches.name: MX Low Profile 2.0 Red

sources.title: Cherry: MX Low Profile 2.0 Red product page
Cherry datasheet: MX Low Profile 2.0 Red
Cherry press release: New standards for low-profile mechanical typing (2025-04-29)
Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Low Profile

switches.notes: Part MX2B-L2NA, 11.9 mm tall, RGB housing; first used in the Cherry KC 500 MX LP keyboards (2025).

switches.name: MX Low Profile 2.0 Speed

sources.title: Cherry: MX Low Profile 2.0 Speed product page
Cherry datasheet: MX Low Profile 2.0 Speed
Cherry press release: New standards for low-profile mechanical typing (2025-04-29)
Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Low Profile

switches.notes: Part MX2B-52NA, 11.9 mm tall, RGB housing with a silver stem.

switches.name: MX Multipoint Black

sources.title: Cherry: MX Multipoint Black product page

switches.notes: Inductive analog switch (part MXID-11NA) with a software-set actuation point; works only with dedicated Multipoint PCBs.

switches.name: MX Multipoint Cyan

sources.title: Cherry: MX Multipoint Cyan product page

switches.notes: Inductive analog switch (part MXID-P1NA) with a progressive spring whose force rises through the travel; works only with dedicated Multipoint PCBs.

switches.name: MX Multipoint Silver

sources.title: Cherry: MX Multipoint Silver product page

switches.notes: Inductive analog switch (part MXID-51NA), the light one of the three; works only with dedicated Multipoint PCBs.

switches.name: MX ULP Click
aka: Cherry MX Ultra Low Profile Click

sources.title: Cherry: MX Ultra Low Profile Click product page
Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Ultra Low Profile

switches.notes: SMD-soldered scissor-type switch (part MX6C-K3NB), 3.9 mm tall per Cherry; used in Alienware m15/m17 R4 laptops and the Corsair K100 Air.

switches.name: MX ULP Tactile
aka: Cherry MX Ultra Low Profile Tactile

sources.title: Cherry: MX Ultra Low Profile Tactile product page
Deskthority wiki: Cherry MX Ultra Low Profile

switches.notes: SMD-soldered scissor-type switch (part MX6C-T3NB) without the click, 3.9 mm tall per Cherry.

switches.name: MX Blossom

sources.title: Cherry Xtrfy shop: CHERRY MX BLOSSOM SWITCHES
Cherry press release: CHERRY leads the revolution from mechanical to smart switches (2025-05-20)

switches.notes: Cherry calls it its lightest linear mechanical switch (part MX2A-LC9D), with an RGB housing.

switches.name: MX Falcon

sources.title: Cherry Xtrfy shop: CHERRY MX FALCON SWITCHES
Cherry press release: CHERRY leads the revolution from mechanical to smart switches (2025-05-20)

switches.notes: Cherry's first long-pole MX switch (part MX2A-HCAD), a heavy tactile with a shortened 3.5 mm travel.

switches.name: MX Northern Light

reviews.verdict: Smooth silent linears that barely change after break-in, though less well and evenly lubed than rival silent linears.

sources.title: Cherry: MX Northern Light product page
Cherry Xtrfy shop: CHERRY MX NORTHERN LIGHT SWITCHES
ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Northern Light Switch Review

switches.notes: Silent linear (part MX2A-8C7D) with a two-part anthracite stem taken from the MX Silent Black.

switches.name: MX Petal

reviews.verdict: Decent light tactiles with a sharper-than-usual bump and soft spring, but some scratch, uneven sound and stem wobble.

sources.title: ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Petal Switch Review

switches.notes: Light tactile (part MX2A-GCBD) with an RGB housing.

switches.name: MX2A Black

reviews.verdict: A modest step up from older MX Blacks in smoothness and spring ping, but still scratchy until well broken in.

sources.title: Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Black Switches

switches.notes: Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX2A Blue

sources.title: Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Blue Switches

switches.notes: Per Cherry, the MX2A Blue keeps its click mechanism without the MX2A factory lube and barrel spring. Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX2A Brown

sources.title: Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Brown Switches

switches.notes: Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX2A Ergo Clear

sources.title: Cherry: MX Ergo Clear product page

switches.notes: The first MX Ergo Clear (MX1A-H1Nx) came out in 2022. Cherry's datasheet lists a 40 cN pressure point while its page and telcontar.net give 55 cN; 55 is kept.

switches.name: MX2A Honey

reviews.verdict: A strong, early bump undone by scratch, weak dampening and loud housing noise; feels unfinished for a silent tactile.

sources.title: Cherry Xtrfy shop: CHERRY MX2A HONEY SWITCHES
Cherry press release: CHERRY leads the revolution from mechanical to smart switches (2025-05-20)

switches.notes: Cherry's first silent tactile MX switch, with an Ergo Clear-based silenced stem. The 2025 press release claims over 100 million keystrokes; the product pages say 50 million.

switches.name: MX2A Orange

reviews.verdict: Decent medium-heavy linears and better than older Cherry linears, held back by uneven factory lube and leftover scratch.

sources.title: ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Orange Switch Review

switches.notes: Cherry calls it a reissue of the rare original MX Orange. The per-part datasheet pages give 55 cN; the datasheet summary table says 45 cN.

switches.name: MX2A Purple

reviews.verdict: A competent, subdued medium tactile that feels almost identical to the MX Ergo Clear, underwhelming for its hype and price.

sources.title: ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Purple Switch Review

switches.notes: ThereminGoat reviewed it as a Glarses x Cherry collaboration. The per-part datasheet page and the highlights give 35 cN; the datasheet summary table says 45 cN.

switches.name: MX2A Red

sources.title: Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Red Switches

switches.notes: Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX2A Silent Black

sources.title: Cherry: MX2A Silent Black product page

switches.notes: Cherry's highlights and the MX2A-81NA datasheet page give 60 cN; the property table repeats the Silent Red's 45 cN and red stem.

sources.title: Cherry: MX2A Silent Red product page
Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Silent Red Switches

switches.notes: Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX2A Speed Silver

sources.title: Cherry: MX2A Speed Silver product page
Cherry press release: CHERRY MX2A, exceeding expectations (2023-08-24)
Cherry Xtrfy shop: Cherry MX2A Speed Silver Switches

switches.notes: Sold with and without PCB fixing pins, and in RGB (translucent housing) and non-RGB versions.

switches.name: MX Emerald Reef

reviews.verdict: Forceful, snappy silent tactiles with almost no stem wobble; the only real flaw is a slight sandy scratch through the bump.

sources.title: Cherry: MX Emerald Reef product page
ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Emerald Switch Review

switches.notes: Silent tactile on the MXAA platform (part MXAA-JCCD) with an integrated lens in the top housing.

switches.name: MX Illuma Brown

reviews.verdict: A big step back for Cherry: poor push feel, heavy stem wobble and harsh sound, weak value even at a low price.

sources.title: Cherry: MX Illuma Brown product page
ThereminGoat: Cherry MX Lumina Brown Switch Review

switches.notes: RGB switch on the MXAA platform, sold with (MXAA-G1LB) or without (MXAA_G1NB) an integrated lens; ThereminGoat reviewed part MXAA-G1LB as "Lumina Brown".

switches.name: MX Illuma Red

sources.title: Cherry: MX Illuma Red product page

switches.notes: RGB switch on the MXAA platform, sold with (MXAA-L1LB) or without (MXAA_L1NB) an integrated lens.

switches.name: Viola
switches.notes: Low-cost plate-mounted switch with MX keycap mount whose leaf shorts contacts on the PCB; shown at CES 2020 and used in Corsair K60 Pro keyboards. Absent from Cherry's switch pages; Deskthority records 2023 reports that it was discontinued.
